children: New Delhi, Oct. 18 -- IDBI Bank shares are likely to remain in focus on Monday, October 19, after the lender reported a 39% year-on-year decline in standalone net profit for the September quarter of FY27, largely reflecting the absence of a one-time gain recorded in the year-ago period.
Investors will assess the bank's earnings performance alongside the proposed Fairfax acquisition deal when trading resumes on Monday.
IDBI Bank stock rose 0.80%, or Rs.0.67, to close at Rs.84.12 on Friday. However, it remains down 18.98% year to date.

The Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC)-controlled lender reported a net profit of Rs.2,205 crore for the second quarter ended September 2026, compared with Rs.3,627 crore in the corresponding period last year.

The year-ago profit included a one-time gain of Rs.1,698.96 crore from the sale of the bank's strategic investment in National Securities Depository Ltd (NSDL). IDBI Bank had offered more than 2.22 crore equity shares, representing an 11.11% stake in NSDL, in its initial public offering at an issue price of Rs.799.87 per share.
IDBI Bank's total income increased to Rs.9,865 crore in the September quarter from Rs.9,594 crore a year earlier, according to its regulatory filing.

Interest income rose to Rs.8,512 crore from Rs.7,104 crore in the year-ago quarter. Net interest income (NII), which represents the difference between interest earned and interest paid, increased 29% to Rs.4,228 crore from Rs.3,285 crore.
However, non-interest income declined 46% to Rs.1,353 crore from Rs.2,489 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Operating profit consequently fell to Rs.2,893 crore from Rs.3,523 crore.
The decline in non-interest income and the absence of the previous year's exceptional gain weighed on the bank's reported profitability despite growth in core interest earnings.
Asset quality improves
The bank reported an improvement in asset quality during the quarter.
Gross non-performing assets (NPAs) declined to 2.12% of gross advances at the end of September 2026 from 2.65% a year earlier. Net NPAs fell to 0.17% from 0.21% over the same period.
IDBI Bank has undertaken a significant balance-sheet cleanup in recent years, supported by capital infusion and recoveries that helped reduce bad loans and restore profitability.
The earnings announcement comes days after the government approved the sale of a combined 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax Financial Holdings, led by Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa.

The proposed transaction, approved on October 14, is valued at approximately Rs.52,878 crore, or around $5.5 billion. It involves the sale of the government's 30.48% stake for about Rs.26,620 crore and LIC's 30.24% holding for approximately Rs.26,440 crore.
Fairfax will pay Rs.81 per share, above the benchmark fair value of Rs.75.99 determined by two independent valuation agencies.

The disinvestment process began in 2022 but faced a setback earlier this year after initial bids fell below the government's reserve price. The transaction is expected to be completed before the end of the current financial year.
The deal would represent a major milestone in India's banking privatisation efforts and a significant foreign investment in the domestic banking sector.
On Saturday, the Finance Ministry said there was no legal restriction under the IDBI (Repeal) Act, 2003, preventing the government from reducing or selling its stake in the bank.
The ministry cited a 2018 Delhi High Court judgment that upheld the Centre's authority to dilute its shareholding.

Meanwhile, Watsa is betting on India's economic growth and the bank's transformation to generate long-term returns from the acquisition. Known for his value-investing approach, he told The Economic Times that India's prime minister would make the country "more business friendly"
"You're going to get an economic boom in India for the next 10 years, I think, of very significant proportions," he said.
